Baseline function, life-limiting illness, multiorgan failure

Loss of all brainstem reflexes — consider brain death evaluation
Clinical seizures — EEG and treat

Confounders present; predictors indeterminate
Unexplained coma, subtle twitching
Absent brainstem reflexes and apnea

Suppressed or burst-suppression background ≥72 h, unconfounded = moderately reliable (NCS)
Bilaterally absent N20 with preserved Erb's point and cervical responses = reliable

entries.title: Brain death / death by neurologic criteria (adult)

keyHistory: Mechanism of catastrophic brain injury and time of injury
Hypoxic-ischemic injury: time since arrest
Temperature management and rewarming time
CNS-depressant drugs (including pentobarbital) and paralytics; renal/hepatic function
Chronic hypercarbia (COPD, OSA) and baseline PaCO2
keyExam: Unresponsive to visual, auditory and tactile stimulation
Absent pupillary, corneal, oculocephalic, oculovestibular, cough and gag reflexes
No brain-mediated motor responses (spinal reflexes allowed)
redFlags: Any breath during apnea testing — does not meet criteria
Primary posterior fossa injury without supratentorial catastrophic injury
Unmet prerequisites (BP, temperature, drugs, metabolic)

clues: All prerequisites met; full exam and apnea test consistent
Recent CNS depressants, renal/hepatic failure, no train-of-four twitches
Core temperature ≤36°C or recently rewarmed
Uncorrected labs
Preserved vertical eye movements; peripheral process

workup.test: Neuroimaging consistent with mechanism and severity
notes: Must show catastrophic supratentorial injury if the primary injury is in the posterior fossa

workup.test: Core temperature, BP, electrolytes, glucose, ABG
notes: Correct severe derangements first

Apnea test after the final examination
Ancillary test: 4-vessel catheter angiography, radionuclide CBF scan, or TCD (adults)

notes: Unacceptable: EEG, evoked potentials, CTA, MRA, MRI

decisionRules.condition: Hypoxic-ischemic injury (e.g., cardiac arrest), age ≥24 months
decisionRules.recommendation: Observe ≥24 h after the injury before starting the evaluation
Core temperature >36°C; wait ≥24 h after rewarming to 36°C if temperature was lowered
SBP ≥100 mm Hg and MAP ≥75 mm Hg (or near chronic baseline if it differs substantially)
Minimum of 1 exam in adults, but 2 independent exams by 2 clinicians recommended; clinicians involved in organ recovery may not participate
PaCO2 ≥60 mm Hg AND ≥20 mm Hg above pre-test baseline AND arterial pH <7.3; with known chronic hypercarbia, ≥20 above the chronic baseline
Pre-test PaCO2 35–45 mm Hg unless known chronic hypercarbia

Only when exam/apnea can't be completed or interpreted, after performing all testable elements; not for hypothermia, high CNS-depressant levels, or skull defects/CSF diversion alone; never if any finding shows brain-mediated activity
